item.title: TT-104: Undo
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog (the Python package is in tasktracker/, tests in tests/). Implement ticket TT-104 from BACKLOG.md exactly as written there.

Ticket TT-104: Undo
`tasktracker.store.TaskStore` has `add`, `complete` and `delete`. Add `undo()`:
- It reverts the most recent not-yet-undone `add`, `complete` or `delete`; repeated calls walk further back (LIFO), across all three kinds.
- Undoing an `add` removes that task; undoing a `complete` makes the task open again; undoing a `delete` restores the task exactly as it was, under the same id.
- Ids are never reused, even after undoing an `add`.
- With nothing left to undo, `undo()` raises `NothingToUndo` (defined in `tasktracker.store`).
- Failed operations (e.g. completing an unknown id) are not recorded.

Constraints: standard library only. Keep existing tests passing: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`. Add unit tests for every acceptance point above. Keep functions under 60 lines and follow the existing code style. Change only what TT-104 needs. Commit only this ticket's work, as one commit, using the repository's configured git identity, with the trailer line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Do not mention Claude Code, Archon or any tool in the commit message. Stay in your workspace; do not ask questions of the operator.

item.title: TT-103: Search query syntax
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog (the Python package is in tasktracker/, tests in tests/). Implement ticket TT-103 from BACKLOG.md exactly as written there.

Ticket TT-103: Search query syntax
`tasktracker.search.search(tasks, query)` only does a case-sensitive substring match on titles. Support a small query language instead:
- The query is split into terms on whitespace, except inside double quotes: `"fix login"` is one phrase term. All terms must match (AND).
- A bare word or phrase matches when it appears in the title, case-insensitively.
- `tag:NAME` matches tasks that have the tag NAME (exact tag, case-insensitive).
- `status:open` / `status:done` match on status.
- Any other `field:value` term, an unknown status, or an unterminated quote raises `QueryError` (defined in `tasktracker.search`).
- An empty or blank query matches every task. Results keep the input order.

Constraints: standard library only. Keep existing tests passing: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`. Add unit tests for every acceptance point above. Keep functions under 60 lines and follow the existing code style. Change only what TT-103 needs. Commit only this ticket's work, as one commit, using the repository's configured git identity, with the trailer line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Do not mention Claude Code, Archon or any tool in the commit message. Stay in your workspace; do not ask questions of the operator.

item.title: TT-102: RFC 4180 CSV export
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog (the Python package is in tasktracker/, tests in tests/). Implement ticket TT-102 from BACKLOG.md exactly as written there.

Ticket TT-102: RFC 4180 CSV export
`tasktracker.export.to_csv(tasks)` joins fields with commas and breaks on titles containing commas, quotes or newlines. It must produce RFC 4180 CSV:
- Header `id,title,tags,status,due`; one row per task in the given order.
- Tags joined with `;`, due date as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` or empty.
- A field containing a comma, double quote, CR or LF is wrapped in double quotes, with embedded double quotes doubled. Other fields are not quoted.
- Every line (header included) ends with CRLF.

Keep functions under 60 lines and follow the existing code style. Change only what TT-102 needs. item.title: TT-101: Reject impossible due dates
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog (the Python package is in tasktracker/, tests in tests/). Implement ticket TT-101 from BACKLOG.md exactly as written there.

Ticket TT-101: Reject impossible due dates
`tasktracker.dates.parse_due(text, today)` silently clamps impossible dates: `2026-02-30` becomes `2026-02-28`. Instead:
- An impossible calendar date (`2026-02-30`, `2025-02-29`, `2026-04-31`, `2026-13-01`, `2026-00-10`) raises `InvalidDate`, a `ValueError` subclass defined in `tasktracker.dates`, whose message contains the original text.
- Anything else that does not match a supported form also raises `InvalidDate` (today it raises a bare `ValueError`).
- Relative offsets: `+Nd` is N days after `today`, `+0d` is `today`. Negative or unsigned offsets (`-3d`, `3d`) raise `InvalidDate`.
- `today` and `tomorrow` keep working; matching stays case-insensitive and ignores surrounding whitespace.

Constraints: standard library only. Keep existing tests passing: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`. Add unit tests for every acceptance point above. Keep functions under 60 lines and follow the existing code style. Change only what TT-101 needs. Commit only this ticket's work, as one commit, using the repository's configured git identity, with the trailer line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Do not mention Claude Code, Archon or any tool in the commit message. Stay in your workspace; do not ask questions of the operator.
